01What is CRYPTORA?

One line: CRYPTORA discovers where cryptography lives in your software, proves each finding with evidence, shows what quantum computers will break first, and plans a safe classical → hybrid → post-quantum migration — all running in your browser.

Thirty seconds: every organisation sits on years of RSA, ECC, AES, SHA, TLS and hardcoded secrets scattered across code, configs, containers and certificates — with no inventory. CRYPTORA scans real files, GitHub repos, pasted code, Dockerfiles, certificates and binaries; builds a Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM); scores quantum + business risk with an interactive Mosca inequality; orders the break-first list; generates a NIST-aligned (ML-KEM / ML-DSA / SLH-DSA) migration roadmap; and exports board-ready reports. You cannot migrate what you cannot see — CRYPTORA makes crypto visible.

02Why — the problem

1. Quantum computers break today’s public-key crypto — it is a when, not an if

Shor’s algorithm breaks RSA, ECC/ECDSA, DH and DSA once a sufficiently large cryptographically-relevant quantum computer exists; Grover’s algorithm halves symmetric/hash strength (AES-128 → ~64-bit, SHA-256 → ~128-bit). NIST has already standardised the replacements — ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) — and agencies (e.g. NSA CNSA 2.0) mandate PQC transition in national-security systems by the early 2030s. Industry timelines are converging on the same decade.

2. “Harvest now, decrypt later” makes waiting dangerous

Adversaries can record encrypted traffic and secrets today and decrypt them when quantum hardware arrives. Mosca’s inequality says it plainly: if (data lifetime + migration time) > threat horizon, migration is already urgent. Data with a 10-year shelf life is exposed now — CRYPTORA computes this interactively per organisation.

3. Nobody has a crypto inventory

Crypto sprawls: legacy RSA-1024 in one microservice, MD5 password hashes in another, an expired SHA-1 certificate, a hardcoded API key in a Dockerfile, DES in a vendor binary. Spreadsheets and tribal knowledge cannot track this. Without discovery + evidence + prioritisation, migration projects stall at step zero. That is the exact gap — discovery-to-roadmap for PQC — that CRYPTORA fills, aligned with SIH problem statement PS-26164.

The 9 detection layers

LayerWhat it doesExample hit
L1 · Regex~35 cryptographic patterns: algorithms, modes, protocols, key sizes, JWT/TLS markersRSA.generate(1024), AES.MODE_ECB, hashlib.md5
L2 · AST-liteStructure-aware call/import parsing for JS/TS & Python — boosts confidence beyond regeximport → call-graph link “this file really calls RSA”
L3 · SecretsHardcoded keys, API tokens, PEM blocks (values redacted on display)API_KEY = "sk-live-…" (shown redacted)
L4 · EntropyShannon entropy per token + whole-file bytes → hidden/obfuscated cryptoHigh-entropy blob that regex cannot name
L5 · Manifestsnpm / PyPI / Go / Cargo / Maven / Gradle parsing → crypto-relevant packagescrypto-js@3.1.9 → capability map
L6 · ContainersDockerfile static analysis: base images, installed crypto libs, leaked secretslibssl1.0 in image, ENV SECRET=…
L7 · CertificatesHand-rolled ASN.1/DER parser: subject, issuer, validity, signature & key algorithmSHA-1 cert expiring in 12 days
L8 · BinariesPrintable-string extraction + crypto marker search in binaries/documents — never executedDES_ecb_encrypt inside a vendor .so
L9 · Risk + CBOMDeterministic scoring, severity, exposure aggregation and CBOM assemblyrisk 100 · CRITICAL · exposure 59/100

Scoring (deterministic — same scan, same numbers, every time)

Each finding gets a 0–100 risk score (algorithm weakness × key size × exposure × confidence), a severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info), a quantum flag (Shor-breakable / Grover-weakened / safe / PQC) and a confidence %. Findings roll up into file, algorithm and portfolio exposure. Business context (data lifetime, migration time, threat horizon) feeds Mosca’s inequality and re-orders the break-first queue. The roadmap then maps each legacy primitive to its NIST PQC successor in phased waves.

Honesty rule enforced in code: with no scan, every page shows “No scan yet”. Empty result sets render “none found”. Secret values are redacted. The engine never invents rows to look impressive — a claim the jury can verify live by scanning an empty file.

07Difficulties faced & how we solved them

False positives drowned real findings (lockfiles, minified bundles, build output).
Built an exclusion engine: lockfiles (*-lock.json, *.lock, go.sum) and minified/build artefacts are skipped with user-visible toggles and honest “excluded: N” counters in the live log. Precision first, then recall.
Regex alone cannot tell import RSA (unused) from RSA.generate() (real usage).
Added AST-lite: lightweight structural call/import parsing for JS/TS and Python that confirms real usage and raises confidence (e.g. 97% on confirmed calls) — without shipping a full parser per language.
Big repos could freeze a browser tab.
Bounded the work: 40-file GitHub cap with clear messaging, per-file timeouts, streaming progress into the live log, and ZIP/folder intake via JSZip so large private codebases scan offline without any upload.
Secrets vs noise: how to flag keys without leaking them or crying wolf?
Layered signals (patterns + PEM structure + entropy + context) with severity tiers, and values always redacted in UI and exports. A finding says where and what kind — never the secret itself.
Certificates and binaries with zero native dependencies?
Hand-rolled a minimal ASN.1/DER reader for X.509 fields and a printable-strings extractor with crypto-marker search for binaries/documents. Static inspection only — the engine never executes anything it scans.
Backend URL broke across environments (localhost vs preview vs Docker vs public domain).
Implemented environment auto-detection (preview → derived API host, local → localhost:8000, prod → same-origin /api) plus a visible manual override on the Sign-in page. Verified in all four environments.
Users felt the app was “stuck” after starting a scan (drawer blocked the view).
Reworked the flow: the drawer now auto-closes and jumps to the live scan dashboard the moment the engine starts, with a “Watch live” escape hatch mid-fetch. Verified by scripted browser tests.
“Prove it’s really scanning” — the credibility problem every demo faces.
Three answers: (1) deterministic engine — same input, same finding IDs and scores, reproducible on stage; (2) evidence drawers — every row expands to matched code; (3) hostile self-tests — empty file → zero findings; md5(x) added → exactly one new F-ID. The jury can run these live.

08Tackling jury questions

A · Product & purpose

What problem are you solving, in one minute?
Organisations must migrate to post-quantum cryptography this decade but have no inventory of where crypto lives. CRYPTORA discovers it, proves it with evidence, scores quantum risk, and generates the migration plan. No inventory → no migration; we are step zero, done right.
▶ Demo move: Overview numbers → CBOM evidence → Roadmap. 60 seconds.
Who is the user? Who pays?
Users: AppSec engineers, auditors, CISOs. Payers: enterprises facing CNSA 2.0 / compliance deadlines and consultancies selling PQC-migration assessments. The demo is free; the roadmap monetises via team workspaces, CI gates and scheduled drift monitoring.
Is this just a regex grep with a dashboard?
Regex is layer 1 of 9. AST-lite confirms real usage, entropy finds what regex cannot name, ASN.1 parses real certificates, manifests map dependencies — and L9 turns it into scored, ordered, exportable migration intelligence. A grep cannot produce a CBOM, a Mosca verdict or a phased PQC roadmap.
▶ Demo move: Hidden Encryption page (entropy blob regex missed) + Reports PDF.
What happens with a repo with no crypto at all?
Honest empty states: zero findings, “none found”, gauges at 0 — the engine never invents rows. This is a feature, and we demo it on stage with an empty file.

B · Technical depth

How do you avoid false positives?
Four mechanisms: exclusion engine (lockfiles/minified/build), AST-lite usage confirmation, confidence scoring per finding, and severity tiers. Remaining noise is labelled low-confidence rather than hidden.
How accurate is detection? Did you measure it?
Honest answer: this build is a heuristic static scanner; we validate deterministically (fixed fixtures → fixed finding IDs/scores) and ship demo-fixtures for repeatable checks. We do not claim ML-grade precision/recall numbers we haven’t measured — the evidence drawer lets anyone audit every hit. Formal benchmarking against labelled corpora is explicit roadmap.
Why in-browser instead of a server scanner?
Privacy (source never leaves the machine — huge for banks/healthcare), zero server cost per scan (scales to a classroom on a tiny VM), and offline capability (ZIP/folder scans with no network). The server stores only accounts and metadata.
What about obfuscated, minified or compiled code?
Minified code is excluded from regex noise by default but still entropy-scanned; compiled artefacts go through the binary-strings layer; and Hidden Encryption surfaces high-entropy blobs regardless of readability. Full deobfuscation/AST-per-language is roadmap, stated openly.
How does the 40-file GitHub cap affect real repos?
It bounds unauthenticated rate limits (60 req/hr/IP) and browser memory; the cap, skip counts and rate-limit errors are all shown honestly in the live log. Private/large codebases use ZIP or folder upload with no cap and no network. Authenticated GitHub + chunked fetching is roadmap.

C · Cryptography & PQC

Which PQC algorithms do you recommend, and why?
Exactly the NIST standards — ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for key establishment, ML-DSA (FIPS 204) for signatures, SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) where stateless hash-based signatures fit — plus hybrid (classical + PQC) transition paths. We invent no cryptography; the footer of every page says so.
Explain Mosca’s inequality like I’m a CFO.
If your data must stay secret for D years, migration takes M years, and quantum arrives in T years — and D+M > T — then attackers are already harvesting your data to decrypt later. Our calculator turns that into ACT NOW vs NOT YET URGENT with your own numbers.
▶ Demo move: Risk page → drag the three sliders → verdict flips live.
Do you handle symmetric crypto and hashes, or only RSA/ECC?
All three families: asymmetric (RSA/ECC/DH/DSA + key sizes), symmetric (AES incl. ECB/CBC/GCM modes, DES/3DES, ChaCha20), hashes (MD5/SHA-1/SHA-2…), plus TLS/JWT/protocol markers and PQC references (already-migrated code is detected and celebrated, not flagged).
What is a CBOM and why CycloneDX-flavoured?
A Cryptographic Bill of Materials — the machine-readable inventory auditors and tools consume. CycloneDX flavouring keeps exports compatible with the SBOM ecosystem (dependency-track-style pipelines) instead of a proprietary format.

D · Deployment, scale & security

How do I run this? What does it cost?
Three ways: local (npm run dev + uvicorn, 5 min), Docker production (./deploy/deploy.sh, one command), or split static+API hosting. Cost: ₹0 in software; a 1-vCPU/2-GB VM suffices because scanning runs in visitors’ browsers.
▶ Demo move: show the deployment guide + /health + /docs.
Is it safe to scan proprietary code?
Yes by architecture: the engine runs locally, nothing is uploaded (except direct GitHub fetches you explicitly request), secrets are redacted, and scanned code is never executed. The backend only sees accounts and finding metadata.
How do you store passwords and tokens?
bcrypt-hashed passwords, signed JWTs with configurable TTL, Google ID-token verification server-side, and secrets via environment (never committed). OTP is hook-ready with dev-mode echo for demos.

E · Vision & honesty

What doesn’t it do yet?
No full per-language AST, no dynamic analysis, no authenticated GitHub at scale, no team RBAC/CI gates yet — each is on the roadmap. We’d rather show a verified scope than overclaim; everything demoed today is real and reproducible.
What would you build with 3 more months?
(1) Tree-sitter AST per language + SARIF export for CI; (2) GitHub App with chunked large-repo scans + PR comments; (3) team workspaces, scheduled drift monitors and Agility-trend dashboards; (4) labelled-corpus precision/recall benchmark published openly.
Why should we pick you?
Working software over slides: 15 live steps, a real 9-layer engine, one-command deploy, and a demo the jury can attack — scan anything, watch the log, audit every finding, export the PDF. Plus honest engineering: we show our limits alongside our strengths.
